title: Cedarfall integration outreach notebook
content:
Quick context:
Cedarfall is a mid-market workforce training platform (B2B SaaS) with enterprise customers in healthcare and local government. They've been experimenting with an in-house QA model for content indexing but performance/cost has become a blocker. They mentioned data residency requirements for some customers (EU + some state-local privacy rules). Good fit for a Private or Dedicated pilot where we can show latency and cost wins with minimal model changes.

Research notes (public + quick checks):
- HQ: Minneapolis, main infra on GCP (projects appear to be in us-central1 and europe-west1).
- Tech stack: Python, PyTorch models, FastAPI endpoints, Postgres primary, Snowflake analytics, Slack + Gainsight for CS ops.
- Current ML approach: small fine-tuned transformer (in-house) for retrieval-augmented QA. RTX-amp GPU usage spikes on monthly content syncs.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 ok, evaluating HIPAA for a target health system pilot. Legal likely to ask for DPA + data flow diagrams.
- Procurement cadence: typical 60–90 days for new vendors, but engineering pilots can be ~4–6 weeks if security is satisfied.

Who to target (internal mapping):
- Primary: Samir Patel (Head of ML, samir@cedarfall.com) — technical champion
- Secondary: Julia Moreno (Director of Product) — cares about UX latency and costs
- Procurement/Legal: Michael Trent — expects security artifacts
- CS sponsor: Priya Das — owns integration with customers

Hypothesis / outreach angle:
- We can reduce per-query cost by ~40% vs their in-house serving if we route inference to Redwood Dedicated with batching + KV prefix cache.
- Offer: 6-week pilot (no commitment) using Redwood Private (VPC) hosted in their GCP project + limited sample dataset. Deliverables: quant report (latency/cost), example roll-in for 2 product flows, security package.

Sample outbound sequences (A/B test):
A - short technical intro (for Samir)
Subject: Cedarfall QA latency/cost — quick pilot idea
Hey Samir — saw your note on slow QA responses in the community thread. I think we can show a 30–50% cost reduction and sub-200ms tail latency for your current query mix using a Dedicated + KV cache profile. Would you be open to a 30-min call next week to map a 4–6 week pilot?
(CTA: calendar links / propose 30-min slot)

B - product/exec intro (for Julia)
Subject: Faster trainee QA flows for Cedarfall — pilot proposal
Julia — quick one: teams like yours use Redwood to get predictable latency and lower per-query cost while keeping content inside customer VPCs. Simple pilot: we run your top 100 queries and show before/after latency + cost. 6 weeks, low friction. Do you have a contact on the ML side I should loop in?

Call script (first 10 minutes):
1) Brief intros (30s)
2) Pain validation: "Tell me about the spikes — frequency, SLOs, cost pain" (2 mins)
3) Quick wiring diagram readout: "where is data stored, any PII/PHI, do you need on-prem or VPC?" (2 mins)
4) Pitch pilot in plain language: what we will measure and what success looks like (2 mins)
5) Next steps: sample data export, security questionnaire, stakeholder sync (1 min)

Objection handling cheat-sheet:
- "We can keep it in-house": Acknowledge; show measurable metric comparison and offer a no-commit pilot so they can compare actual numbers.
- "Data residency / PHI concerns": Redwood Private in their GCP project or on-prem package; we provide KMS/HSM integration and an SOC2/HIPAA-ready compliance pack.
- "We can't change model weights": Fine. We can serve their existing weights via our runtime (docker + model artifact upload) and still get batching/kv/caching benefits.
- "Cost" (procurement): Flexible pilot pricing, month-to-month Dedicated demo credits, and a clear value statement: cost-per-query reduction + developer time saved.

Pilot success metrics (suggested):
- 95th percentile latency <= 200ms for short QA queries
- Cost per query reduced by >= 30%
- No customer-facing regressions on 10 sample prompts (quality check)
- Security clearance: legal signoff on DPA + network diagram

Internal asks (actions for me / Ben / Lena):
- Ben: prepare a rough benchmark using a small transformer with Cedarfall-like token distributions (deadline: 11/12).
- Lena: pull SOC2 / security pack + HIPAA guidance for PS to include in LOI (deadline: 11/07).
- Me (Aisha): draft pilot one-pager + 2 outbound email variants and set up tracking sheet (deadline: 11/06).

Open questions / risks to surface:
- Do they have a model artifact management process (MLflow)? If not, artifact transfer might be manual and require legal/ops sign-off.
- Are there live customers with PHI in the training data? If yes, pilot needs strict isolation and extra legal review.
- Who owns product KPIs for the trainee flows — CS or product? helps scope success metrics.

Quick checklist before first outreach:
- [ ] Pilot one-pager (Aisha)
- [ ] Security pack + DPA template (Lena)
- [ ] Benchmark sample (Ben)
- [ ] 30-min intro calendar draft and A/B email text loaded into Outreach sequence

Notes to self: keep initial ask simple — measure latency and run a cost delta. Emphasize safety: we can run everything inside their GCP project if needed. Stay light on pricing in first touch; focus on measurable pilot outcomes.

Example closing line for email: "If you can share a small sample of your query logs we’ll run a head-to-head and send a short report — no install required. Thoughts?"

-- end of notebook --
